prompt.text:
Create `solution.py` with a top-level function `collect_entries(pages)` that extracts ranked catalogue entries from in-memory HTML fragments using only the standard library.

`pages` must be an iterable of strings. Each entry is an `<article>` element with attributes `data-rank` and `data-score`, containing one `<h2>` title and zero or more `<span class="contributor">` elements. Attribute order and unrelated nested markup may vary.

Return a list of dictionaries with keys `rank` (integer), `title` (trimmed visible text), `contributors` (list of trimmed, nonempty contributor texts in document order), and `score` (float). Sort results by ascending rank, regardless of page order.

Skip an article if its rank is not a positive base-10 integer, its score is not finite, or its title is missing or empty. If ranks repeat, retain only the first valid article encountered in the supplied page order. Empty input returns `[]`. A non-string page or malformed HTML that leaves an article unclosed raises `ValueError`. The returned dictionaries and contributor lists must be newly allocated and must not alias parser internals or one another.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
